question: Anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm antibodies are highly specific for SLE, whereas ANA positivity alone is not sufficient to diagnose SLE.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Recall the immunology of SLE. ANA is a screening test with high sensitivity but low specificity. The specific antibodies that point strongly to SLE are anti-dsDNA (also a disease activity marker) and anti-Sm.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. ANA is sensitive (~98%) but not specific for SLE — it is positive in many other conditions. Anti-dsDNA (especially at high titres, correlating with disease activity/lupus nephritis) and anti-Sm are highly specific for SLE and form part of both the ACR and SLICC/ACR classification criteria.
